editorPanel.restingHint: Click a piece to inspect it, or pick a tool to start painting.
editorPanel.allowDynamicArmyHelp: When on, players build their own army for the battle type and deploy it inside their zones. When off, they fight with the units you placed on the map and the army screen is skipped.
editorPanel.fixedRosterHelp: When on, the scenario decides the player slots, the teams, and the ammunition each side gets, and nobody can be added or removed in the lobby. When off, the lobby or matchmaking decides who plays.
editorPanel.allowDeploymentPhaseHelp: When on, the battle opens with one extra turn before any fighting, so each player can rearrange their units inside their deployment zone. When off, the fighting starts at once, with no chance to reposition first.
editorPanel.noInherentAmmoHelp: When on, units start with no ammunition and draw everything from their side's shared reserve, so they cannot fire until the first resupply reaches them. When off, they begin the battle with their own supply as usual.
editorPanel.goBackConfirm: Leave the editor and go back to the menu?

playersPanel.ammoHelp: How much ammunition this player's army has. The reserve is what it spends over the battle, and the base is the level the reserve climbs back toward each turn.

createUnit.title: Create Unit
createUnit.placingCopied: Placing copied units ({{count}}). Click the map to place them.

deployment.title: Deployment zones
deployment.hint: These zones are where each army starts the battle. Switch on the deployment phase and players get one extra turn before the fighting begins, purely to shuffle their units around inside their zone.

formationModal.title: Edit custom formation
formationModal.collisionHelp: The space this formation takes up on the ground. A circle needs only a radius, while a rectangle needs its frontage across the front and its depth from front to back. Set the radius to 0 and the formation takes up no space at all, passing through everything.
formationModal.fireEdgesHelp: Each fire edge emits along one face of the rectangle. A formation with no fire edges fires a default single front edge; circle formations do not fire.
formationModal.errIdInUse: Formation id "{{id}}" is already in use
formationModal.errEdgeIndex: Fire edge {{n}}: edge index must be 0-3
formationModal.errEdgeArc: Fire edge {{n}}: arc must be between 0 and 360
formationModal.errEdgeEmitters: Fire edge {{n}}: emitters must be a positive integer

unitTemplateModal.title: Edit custom unit template
unitTemplateModal.reportStatsHelp: What this unit adds to the tallies in a battle report, such as men, horses, or guns. The categories come from the era's own units.

errors.idInUse: Unit category id "{{id}}" is already in use
errors.orphanedResistances: Resistances point at damage types that do not exist: {{types}}
errors.orphanedAutofire: Autofire priority points at unit categories that do not exist: {{categories}}
errors.allowedOrderRequired: All allowed-order entries must be selected
errors.allowedOrderUnknown: Allowed order "{{name}}" is not a known order for this era

chargeBacklash.description: How hard this category hits back when something charges it. Higher means it braces and strikes back harder, and 0 means it does not hit back at all. The after-running value is used when the defender has already run and cannot brace, and falls back to the base figure. Defaults to 1.

chargeStamina.description: Max stamina a charge drains from this category. The charger pays it in full head-on and less when flanking; a defender pays it in full when flanked, with a 25% floor either way. Defaults to 0 (no cost).

resistances.description: How well this category stands up to each damage type. A negative figure means it takes more damage, a positive figure means it takes less.

autofire.description: Priority weight per target unit category. Higher values are preferred targets for autofire.
autofire.warnOnMaxHint: Warns that ammunition is being wasted when this category fires at its Max tier. Useful for artillery.

errors.idInUse: Damage type id {{id}} is already in use
errors.nameInUse: Damage type name "{{name}}" is already in use
errors.idBelongsToBuiltIn: Damage type id {{id}} belongs to built-in "{{name}}". Keep the name to override it, or pick a different id.
errors.nameBelongsToBuiltIn: Name "{{name}}" belongs to built-in id {{id}}. Set id to {{id}} to override it, or pick a different name.
errors.rangedNeedsBracket: Ranged damage types need at least one range bracket
errors.maxRangeRequired: Max range must be greater than 0
errors.rangeBandBounds: Each band's From/To must be within 0–100%, with From ≤ To.
errors.lastBandMustReachMax: The last band must reach 100% (max range).

targetStat.helper: Measured as a percentage of the target's own stat. Nothing happens above the From figure, the full value applies at or below the To figure, and the effect grows as the target weakens in between.

terrainCategoryModal.title: Edit custom terrain category
terrainCategoryModal.identityHint: This overrides one of the era's terrain categories, for this scenario only. You cannot change which terrains belong to it, since the era fixes that. What you can change is how the category treats the troops standing on it.
terrainCategoryModal.perUnitCategoryHint: Each row sets the value for one kind of troops. The `*` row is the default, used by any kind you have not given a row of its own. Deleting a row that `*` covers will not stick, because it returns the next time you edit. Give that row its own value instead.
terrainCategoryModal.projectileAbsorptionHint: Each row sets the value for one damage type.

errors.idInUse: Terrain category id "{{id}}" is already in use
errors.unknownDamageTypes: Projectile absorption points at damage types that do not exist: {{keys}}

spritesPanel.title: Unit sprites
spritesPanel.description: A sprite is the picture a unit wears on the field. Upload your own and you can pick them when you set up a unit's formations. They ride inside the scenario file itself, so each one has to stay under {{kb}}KB. Upload one below.
spritesPanel.noSprites: None yet, so your units wear the pictures the era already provides.
spritesPanel.maxSpritesAlert: You can keep at most {{count}} sprites in a scenario. Delete one to make room.
spritesPanel.tooLargeAlert: Image too large; could not compress under {{kb}}KB. Try a smaller or simpler image.
spritesPanel.invalidImageAlert: Could not read the image. Use a PNG or WebP file.
spritesPanel.deleteBlockedAlert: You can't delete this sprite while {{where}} still use it. Change those formations first.
spritesPanel.libraryDescription: Every sprite the era already provides, free for you to use. Have a look before you make your own.

unitTemplatesPanel.title: Unit templates
unitTemplatesPanel.description: A template is the blueprint every unit on the map is stamped from. Override one of the era's own to change it for this scenario alone, or clone one to start a unit of your own. Add one below.
unitTemplatesPanel.noTemplates: None yet, so this scenario fields the era's own units.
unitTemplatesPanel.deleteBlocked: You can't delete "{{name}}" while {{refs}} still use it. Remove those first.

formationsPanel.title: Unit formations
formationsPanel.description: A formation is how a unit arranges itself: line, column, square. Every unit you create or edit carries the ones it can use, and switching between them changes how it fights. Add a formation of your own below.
formationsPanel.noFormations: None yet, so your units form up the way the era already allows.
formationsPanel.deleteBlocked: You can't delete "{{id}}" while {{refs}} still use it. Remove those first.

unitCategoriesPanel.title: Unit categories
unitCategoriesPanel.description: A category is the kind of troops a unit is: infantry, skirmishers, artillery. Every unit you create or edit belongs to one, and units sharing a category behave alike. Add one of your own below.
unitCategoriesPanel.noCategories: None yet, so every unit belongs to one of the era's own kinds of troops.
unitCategoriesPanel.deleteBlocked: You can't delete "{{id}}" while {{refs}} still use it. Remove those first.

damageTypesPanel.title: Damage types
damageTypesPanel.description: A damage type decides how a weapon works. Every unit you create or edit has one for melee and can carry several more for shooting at range. Add your own below.
damageTypesPanel.noDamageTypes: None yet, so your units fight with the weapons the era already provides.
damageTypesPanel.deleteBlocked: You can't delete "{{name}}" while {{refs}} still use it. Remove those first.

terrainCategoriesPanel.title: Terrain categories
terrainCategoriesPanel.description: A terrain category is how a patch of ground treats the troops standing on it: what it slows, what it shelters, what it blocks. Override the era's version here and the change applies to this scenario alone. Add an override below.
terrainCategoriesPanel.noOverrides: Nothing overridden yet, so terrain behaves exactly as the era intends.

overrideEditor.structuralTooltip: This one shapes how the game itself runs. Changing it can break how battles are drawn, how replays play back, and how matchmaking works.

importModal.title: Import {{kind}} from scenario
importModal.pickFilePrompt: Choose a scenario file to bring its {{kind}} across. Any scenario you have downloaded from the editor will do.
importModal.fileReadError: That doesn't look like a scenario file. Try another.
importModal.invalidForEra: That scenario's custom definitions don't fit the era you're working in: {{message}}
importModal.importWouldInvalidate: Nothing was imported, because that would have left your scenario invalid: {{message}}
importModal.noCustomDefs: That scenario has no custom {{kind}} to bring across.
importModal.willImport: This will bring across {{summary}}, plus anything they depend on.
importModal.resultSummary: Added {{imported}}. Renamed {{renamed}} that would have clashed. Skipped {{skipped}} you already had.

importOverridesModal.title: Import {{target}} from scenario
importOverridesModal.pickFilePrompt: Choose a scenario file to bring its {{target}} across. Any scenario you have downloaded from the editor will do.

importArmyCompositionsModal.title: Import army compositions from scenario
importArmyCompositionsModal.pickFilePrompt: Choose a scenario file to bring its army compositions across. Any scenario you have downloaded from the editor will do.
importArmyCompositionsModal.noArmyCompositions: This scenario has no army composition settings to import.

gameConstants.title: Game constants
gameConstants.description: These are the era's underlying numbers: how long a turn lasts, how large a tile is, how many turns a battle runs. Anything you change applies to this scenario alone, and Reset puts a value back as you found it. The ones marked ⚠ affect how battles are drawn and replayed, so tread carefully with those.

gameRules.title: Game rules
gameRules.description: These are the systems the era runs on: flanking, stamina, ammunition, supply lines, entrenchment, and the rest. Anything you change applies to this scenario alone, and Reset puts a value back as you found it. The numbers are in the game's own units, so a figure may not read as metres or minutes.

ordersPanel.title: Orders
ordersPanel.description: Orders are the instructions a player can give a unit during a battle. You can retune the era's own orders here for this scenario, though you cannot invent new ones. Reset puts a value back as you found it.

clonePicker.alreadyOverriddenTooltip: This built-in already has a custom override in this scenario; edit it from the list instead.

armyPanelGroups.title: Army panel groups
armyPanelGroups.description: Choose the headings players see when buying an army, which units sit under each, and their order. This starts from the era's default layout.
armyPanelGroups.statusDefault: Untouched. This scenario uses the era's standard army compositions, and editing anything below switches it to a list of your own.
armyPanelGroups.statusCustom: Customised. Players now see only the units you put into a group, and nothing else. Add a new unit to the scenario later and it stays hidden until you group it here too.
armyPanelGroups.statusEraDisabled: The era's own units are switched off, so the standard layout is hidden. Build your groups from this scenario's units below.
armyPanelGroups.noUnits: No units in this group yet.

customArmyCompositions.title: Army compositions
customArmyCompositions.betaNotice: Army compositions are still in beta. If you find a bug, please report it in the official Discord server.
customArmyCompositions.disableEraUnitsDescription: Play with only the units this scenario provides. The era's own units disappear from the army screen and cannot be chosen.
customArmyCompositions.disableEraUnitsWarning: You will want at least one unit template of your own first, or players will have nothing to field.

unitCaps.title: Unit caps
unitCaps.description: Limit how many of each unit a player may field. Add a unit, then set its cap for each battle type. Leave a field empty and the era's own cap applies, which is the number already shown in it. A cap of 0 removes that unit from the battle type entirely.
unitCaps.empty: None yet, so each unit is limited exactly as the era limits it.

battleTypeBudgets.title: Battle-type budgets
battleTypeBudgets.description: Change the manpower and gold each player starts with in each battle type. Leave a field empty and the era's own figure applies, which is the number already shown in it.

playerBudgets.title: Per-player budgets
playerBudgets.description: Give one player a budget of their own, overriding the battle type's for that seat alone. Add a player, then set either figure, and leave one empty to keep the battle-type budget. Players are matched by their seat number in the lobby.
playerBudgets.empty: None yet, so every player gets the battle-type budget.

scale.errorInvalid: Enter a positive width and height, in tiles.
scale.warningBody: It may be worth saving your scenario before you do this. Resizing stretches everything on the map along with it: terrain, heights, units, objectives, and triggers.

expandCut.intro: Positive values add tiles, negative values remove tiles from each side.
expandCut.errorTooSmall: Cannot resize: resulting map would be smaller than 1×1 tiles. Please adjust the values.
expandCut.errorTooLarge: Cannot resize: resulting map would exceed maximum size of {{maxWidth}}×{{maxHeight}} tiles.
expandCut.warningBody: You might want to save your scenario first. Adding or removing tiles moves the map's edges, and anything left outside the new bounds is removed with them.

localesPanel.title: Locales
localesPanel.description: Locales let you translate your scenario, so players read its names and descriptions in their own language. Add a language, then give each piece of text a translation.
localesPanel.noKeys: No translation keys. Add a key to get started.

randomMap.title: Random Map
randomMap.proceduralExplanation: These instructions generate the map from a new seed each match; the saved scenario drops its baked map. The map shown here is only a preview. Objectives placed by Objective / Objective layer instructions appear at match time, not in this preview.
randomMap.noInstructions: No instructions yet. Add one above or load a template.
randomMap.switchToPresetConfirm: Switching to a preset keeps the current terrain and clears the generation instructions. Continue?
randomMap.replaceInstructionsConfirm: Replace the current instructions with the template's?
randomMap.fillFromTemplateDescription: Fill the current map's terrain from a procedural template. This bakes a fixed (preset) map and does not keep any generation instructions.
randomMap.confirmOverwriteLabel: I understand this will overwrite all terrain
randomMap.importMustBeProcedural: That file needs to be a procedural template. It must carry generation instructions and no baked map.
randomMap.invalidJsonFile: That file could not be read. Check that it is a scenario the editor produced.
randomMap.confirmOverwriteWarning: Tick the box to confirm you are happy to overwrite the terrain.
randomMap.selectedNotProcedural: Selected scenario is not a procedural template.
randomMap.hybridExplanation: The baked terrain is kept and these instructions re-run on top of it as overlays each match. Pin a seed on the map to stop the overlays drifting between matches.

randomDeployment.title: Deployment zones
randomDeployment.explanation: Where each team's units start, as percentages of the map. Keep it symmetric for a fair match, or uncheck to author each side.
randomDeployment.noZones: No zones — the generator uses defaults.

scoring.heading: VP weights
scoring.hint: Leave a field empty to use the battle type's own figure, or the era's.
scoring.basePointsInfo: Starting VP both teams get before casualties, objectives, or pressure are applied.
scoring.casualtiesInfo: Max VP from the casualty difference between teams. Higher favours attrition over holding objectives.
scoring.underPressureInfo: VP a team loses per turn while under pressure. 0 disables the penalty.
scoring.pressureThresholdInfo: A team is under pressure while it holds this % of objective VP or less.
scoring.bigDefaultInfo: Fallback VP for a big objective that doesn't set its own value. Individual objectives can still override it.
scoring.smallDefaultInfo: Fallback VP for a small objective that doesn't set its own value. Individual objectives can still override it.
scoring.tieBreakInfo: On the final turn, a team trailing on VP by more than this is treated as defeated.

objectiveZones.heading: Objective zones
objectiveZones.hint: How much to shrink the areas where objectives can be placed. Leave a field empty to use the battle type's own figure, or the era's.
objectiveZones.smallInsetInfo: How much to narrow the small-objective zone on each side. Trims only its width, keeping its vertical reach.
objectiveZones.bigInsetInfo: How much to shrink the big-objective box on each side, centered inside the deployment zone.
